root_causes.description: Constraint validation is implemented as generic string-expression evaluation (regex sanitising plus DataFrame.eval over a full-frame copy) repeated per inequality and per device, so fixed interpretive overhead multiplies with device count.
Pyomo 3-D index set is built by a nested scan of the full commitment-group set for every (commitment, time) pair.

findings.problem: Per-device constraint validation evaluates each inequality through regex column sanitising and two DataFrame.eval calls on a freshly cast copy of the whole frame, up to 14 times per device, so the validation step costs a large fixed amount per device.
findings.performance_principle: Do not pay interpretive, per-call setup costs for work that is a handful of vectorised comparisons; hoist invariant work (type cast, fill, parsing) out of repeated operations.

evidence.statement: _prepare validates every flexible device inside the per-device loop: validate_power_constraints, then validate_storage_constraints when stock validation applies.
validate_constraint calls sanitize_expression for both sides; sanitize_expression runs re.search and re.sub (pattern built per call) for every column of the frame.
validate_constraint does constraints_df.astype(float).fillna(0).eval(...).round(...) separately for lhs and rhs, so the whole frame is copied and cast twice per inequality.
validate_storage_constraints issues up to 11 validate_constraint calls and validate_power_constraints 3 (derived: 3 + 11 = 14 calls, 2 evals each = 28 evals per device).
No runtime evidence (profile, benchmark, trace) exists in the repository or was supplied.

findings.conditions: Matters when a schedule has many devices (the operators' stated symptom) and the solver time per device is small enough that this fixed pandas overhead is a visible share; assumes skip_validation is False. Per-device cost is roughly independent of device count, so total grows linearly with devices; the time horizon only affects vectorised work. Magnitude unknown without a profile.

counter_evidence.statement: Validation is vectorised over time steps, so cost per call does not grow with horizon length; the cost is mostly fixed overhead per call.
Growth is linear in devices, not superlinear; the LP solve is likely to grow faster, so validation may not be the dominant share. Not measurable from source.
A skip_validation switch exists on compute(), so a caller can already bypass it.
Searched _prepare and the validators for cross-device loops (device x device); none found in the validation path.

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: Each device does a fixed, small number of vectorised pandas calls; with realistic device counts the LP solve may dwarf this, and a failed validation avoids an infeasible solve, which is expensive. Without a profile this could be a minor share.
findings.recommendation: Replace the string-expression engine in the validators with direct vectorised comparisons on numpy/pandas columns: cast and fill the frame once per device, compute lhs/rhs with plain arithmetic, and build the violation message text only for rows that fail. Keep the existing violation output format so the error message is unchanged.

alternatives.option: Cache the float-cast, NaN-filled frame once per device and reuse it across the validate_constraint calls, keeping eval.
alternatives.why: Removes the repeated casts but leaves the regex and eval parsing cost.

alternatives.option: Rewrite the validators as direct column arithmetic with lazy message construction.
alternatives.why: Removes parsing, regex and repeated copies, which are the per-call overheads; behaviour is easy to pin with the existing validate_storage_constraints tests.

alternatives.option: Skip validation for devices whose constraint columns are entirely unset.
alternatives.why: Cheap but changes what is checked and does not help dense inputs.

findings.trade_offs: Hand-written comparisons are less declarative than the expression strings and must preserve NaN-skipping and rounding semantics (6 decimals) exactly; a regression there would change which inputs are rejected.

validation.metric: Wall time and call counts of validate_power_constraints plus validate_storage_constraints within one StorageScheduler._prepare for a multi-device flex-model, at several device counts.
validation.expectation: Validation time per device drops and the share of _prepare spent in pandas eval and re.sub decreases; direction only, magnitude to be measured.
validation.falsifier: A profile showing validation is a negligible share of schedule computation time, or that time per device is flat but small relative to the solve.
validation.guard: A micro-benchmark or unit test that asserts identical violation lists before and after the rewrite on the existing test inputs.

commands.purpose: Profile the validators on the existing constraint tests to see the share of eval and regex time (run in a dev checkout, not by this review).

findings.problem: The Pyomo cjg index set is built by iterating, for every (commitment, time) pair, the whole commitment-device-group set and filtering by commitment id, which is O(|cj| x |cg|).
findings.performance_principle: Index by the join key (group by commitment) instead of re-scanning the full relation for each probe.

evidence.statement: commitment_time_device_groups_init: ((c, j, g) for (c, j) in m.cj for (_, g) in m.cg if _ == c) scans all of m.cg for each of the (c, j) pairs.
device_group_lookup already maps commitment to its groups, so a per-commitment lookup is available (used at line 292 for cg).
Reached only when FLEXMEASURES_LP_SOLVER is not highspy, because the highspy backend returns earlier.

findings.conditions: Only for deployments configured with a Pyomo-based solver, and with many commitments (each time step of each commitment contributes a (c,j) pair that scans every (c,g) pair). Commitment count is assumed, not shown, to grow with device count because the scheduler appends per-device commitments (e.g. storage.py:1127, 1338).

counter_evidence.statement: Default backend is highspy, which bypasses this code entirely.
Interchangeable sub-commitments are merged before model build, which reduces the commitment count.
Searched highspy_optimization.py for the same pattern; it consumes device_group_lookup per commitment directly.

findings.recommendation: Build the set from device_group_lookup directly: for each (c, j) in cj, iterate only the groups of c.
findings.trade_offs: Set ordering may differ, which could change Pyomo variable ordering and solver tie-breaking among equal-cost solutions; negligible complexity.

validation.metric: Time to construct model.cjg for a Pyomo-configured multi-device schedule.
validation.expectation: Construction time grows linearly rather than quadratically with commitment count; direction only.
validation.falsifier: Deployments use highspy, or construction time is negligible in a profile.
validation.guard: A test that the set of cjg tuples is unchanged by the rewrite.

considered_not_reported.observation: _validate_commitments_are_enforceable and the commitment-group construction loops in scheduling_problem.py.
considered_not_reported.why_discarded: Linear in sub-commitments with array reads; no repeated scans found. A source comment in scheduling_problem.py already records an earlier optimisation of this loop.
considered_not_reported.revisit_when: A profile shows model-preparation time rather than validation or the solve dominating.
